description: The Combined Drought Indicator is a gridded early warning layer designed to monitor agricultural drought. The JRC Data Catalogue page read on 2026-09-26 says it combines precipitation (SPI), soil moisture and fAPAR vegetation greenness anomalies into three drought classes (Watch, Warning, Alert) and three recovery classes. It is published by the European Commission Joint Research Centre for the European Drought Observatory of the Copernicus Emergency Management Service, under the CC BY 4.0 licence, free of charge with no registration (access conditions: no limitations). Data run from January 2012 onward, updated three times a month as ten-day files, served as yearly NetCDF and zip files in a download folder and as a WMS map layer. Coverage is Europe (the WMS uses a European projection; the exact extent is not stated on the page read). Caveats: the folder README says version 4.1.1 replaced 4.1.0 in July 2026 when the fAPAR input moved from Suomi NPP to NOAA-21, and files ending in pNN are provisional until a final zMM file replaces them. For simulation it gives dekadal drought hazard states to drive crop loss, irrigation demand and supply chain disruption scenarios for European agriculture and industry. Related catalogue records include the ERA5 reanalysis and the drought index datasets written in this batch, such as the Brazilian Integrated Drought Index.
